description_en: Locally known as Saĩthu Gaṇeśa, this two-roofed south facing Gaṇeśa temple is situated in the Ḍhokāsi Ṭola of Patan. In the late Malla period, this temple area was the northern entrance (palaṃ dhvākhā) of the Patan kingdom. The temple is called Sainyathuri Gaṇeśa in an inscription (LAL1490_I_20181203_10.JPG) of that period.Surrounded by a handful of smaller temples and open shrines, this main temple occupies a rectangular base of 432 x 254 cm and is located to the north of the plaza (see site plan). Residential houses surround the plaza on the northern, southern and western sides, while a vehicular road passes by to the east.The thick brick walls open up to a colonnaded entrance at the west, which is flanked by two stone statues of lions. Surrounding the temple is a brick wall topped with iron rod made fence. People from Cvabũ and Gaḥchẽ Ṭola worship Saĩthu Gaṇeśa as their local deity. Unlike other Gaṇeśa temples of the Kathmandu Valley it is constructed in a rectangular shape. It is exclusive that animal sacrifice (bali) is offered to Saĩthu Gaṇeśa in Daśaĩ festival while it is generally offered to the deities of the Śākta tradition. The temple has two stories, with 16 plain struts in each tier. Each level has carved windows on each sides.Four side struts of the temple exhibit the images ofśārdūlas, while the rest are plain. A long metal banner (patāḥ)with an image of standing Gaṇeśa at the bottom hangs from the middle pinnacle of the temple all the way down to thetoraṇaatthe main entrance. A small temple made of bronze can be found within the bigger temple, inside which is an aniconic image of Gaṇeśa. A newly made copperkīrtimukha toraṇahas been fixed above the entrance of the sanctum, which contains an image of four handed Gaṇeśa sitting inlalitaposture, holding axe, garland, carrot and sweet balls.Inside the temple courtyard, there is a Gorakhanātha shrine, a Bhairava shrine, a Sūryavināyaka temple, ahiṭī, aphalcā(which has now been turned into a private house),a sataḥand three shrines of family gods.According to locals, the open shrines with aniconic images at various elevations (as seen in the site plan), aredigudyaḥlocations of the people of different areas of Patan.Another important monument is the temple of Sūryavināyaka located at the eastern entry of the plaza. The aniconic shrine is roofed and the main sanctum is raised 195 cm from the ground. A single storeysataḥis attached to the main temple complex on the eastern side. This is mostly used during local feasts and festivals. There is agā hitī(stepped stone water conduit) to the northeastern side of the plaza which will be documented as a separate monument.
description_ne: यो मन्दिर पाटनको ढोकासि टोलमा रहेको छ । उत्तर मल्ल कालमा यस टोलमा उत्तरतर्फबाट पाटनमा प्रवेश गर्ने ढोका (पलं ध्वाखा) थियो ।  उत्तर दिशाबाट पाटन शहर प्रवेश गर्ने मल्लकालीन ढोका (पलं ध्वाखा) आसपासको क्षेत्रलाई ढोकासि भनिन्छ । यस गणेशलाई स्थानीयले ''सैँथु गणेश'' भन्दै आएका छन् । यहाँ रहेको उत्तरमल्लकालीन शिलालेखमा यस गणेशलाई ''सैन्यथुरि गणेश'' भनिएको छ । त्यसताका नै गणेशलाई सम्बोधन गर्ने यो शब्द प्रचलनमा रहेको बुझिन्छ । पाटनको च्वबुँ र गःछेँ टोलका स्थानीयले यस गणेशलाई स्थानगणेशको रूपमा पूज्दै आएका छन् । उपत्यकाका अन्य गणेश मन्दिरहरू आयताकार संरचनामा पाइँदैनन् तर अपवादस्वरूप यो दुईतले गणेश मन्दिर आयताकार छ । शक्तिपीठमा जस्तै दशैँमा यस गणेशलाई बलि दिने पृथक् परम्परा पनि रहिआएको छ । गणेशकोअमूर्तप्रतिमालाईबीचमाराखीपित्तलकोसानोमन्दिरस्वरूपकोसंरचनामाबनाइएकोछ ।मन्दिरकोथामोमाथिनिदालमाहालसालैनिर्मिततामाकोकीर्तिमुखतोरणचढाइएकोछ।तोरणकोबीचभागमाचारहातभएकागणेशललितासनमाबसेकाछन्।दक्षिणाभिमुखयस मन्दिरलाईपर्खाललेघेरीढोकाबनाइएकोछरढोकाकोदायाँ-बायाँएकजोडासिंहस्थापितछ।मन्दिरमागणेशमानीपूजिनेअमूर्तमूर्तिदक्षिणतिरफर्काईराखिएकोछ।मन्दिरमागजूरदेखितल्लोछानासम्मपुग्नेपताःचढाइएकोछ।पताःकोतल्लोकिनारमाउभिएका गणेशकोमूर्तिकुँदिएकोछ।उक्तगणेशकोचारहातमध्येमाथिल्लोदुईहातलेपरशुरअक्षमालात्यसै गरीतल्लोदुईहातलेमुलारलड्डुसमाउँदैगरेकोदेखाइएकोछ।चारकुनाका टुँडालमाकुंसल(शार्दूल)का मूर्ति कुँदिएका छन् भने बाँकी सबैटुँडालहरूसादाछन्।मन्दिरकोछानामाथि३वटाधातुकागजूरछन्।यस मन्दिरपरिसरमागोरखनाथदेवल,भैरवदेवल,सूर्यविनायकदेवल,हिटी,फल्चा(हालव्यक्तिगरणभईघरनिर्माणभैसकेको),सतःरतीनवटाकुलदेवतादेवलहरूरहेकाछन्।

references: Sources and references Sources According to inscription from NS 1124

historical_events.event_description: Virapati Jogi and his wife Madhari Jogini renovated the shrine.

historical_events.event_name: Stone statues of devotees, made on a single stone was attached to the northern wall of the Gorakhanāta Shrine
historical_events.event_description: The images of Punāvatī, Saṅṣadāsa, Punasvarī and Acikitī's have been installed.

The inscription mentions that Darśandhāri Rāmdāsa Jogīhad established an image but it is not clear which image it is. Inside the Gorakhanātha shrine beside the inscription there are images of stone devotees. It is possible that these images were installed by him.
Kisalāla Maharjan, Nānimāyā, Nhuccheñmāyā and their family reconstructed the Sūryavināyaka shrine.

historical_events.event_name: Coral studded golden feet (pādukā) was offered to the Gorakhanātha
historical_events.event_description: Darśandhāri Pvaṁca Jugi donated coral-studded golden feet (pādukā) to Gorakhanātha.
Jayañta Maharjan and Bāla Kṛṣṇa Maharjan, sons of the late Śuṣālāla Maharjan, donated thetoraṇa.
The entrance was reconstructed in the name of late Herākāji, most probably by his family members.
Thekuladevatāshrine was restored by the Kuladevatā Mandira Jīrṇoddhāra Samiti.

historical_events.event_name: A patāḥ made of brass was hanged on the Gaṇeśa temple
historical_events.event_description: Silāl, Matimāyā and the Maharjan family hung a brasspatāḥon the Gaṇeśa temple.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a pāṭī/sattal behind the Gaṇeśa temple
historical_events.event_description: Thepāṭī/sattalwas constructed by the local community.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a pātī/sattal behind the Gaṇeśa temple
historical_events.event_description: Dhanamāyā Maharjan, Kṛṣṇa Maharjan and their family constructed apātī/sattalbehind the Gaṇeśa temple.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a shrine of a family deity
historical_events.event_description: Jagata Siñ Bhāvo, Jugi Rāma Bhāvo and other Bhāvos constructed a shrine. Relying upon the inscription (LAL1490_I_20181203_06.JPG),Pruscha(1975,170) assumes that the Gaṇeśa temple was constructed in 1681. However, the inscription suggests that some other shrine was constructed at the date. Regarding the object, only the last letter of the word ( ‘ri’ ) is retained in the inscription; the first two letters of the word are effaced. With this in mind,Siṃha(2018, XX) postulates that the rubbed word is‘gajuri’(i.e. pinnacle), but that it could also be read as‘deguri’(a temple of family deity) because there are several such shrines in this temple area.
On the south-west corner of the temple and above the wooden pillar, a lintel is embossed with the numbers '1997'. This suggests that the temple was reconstructed on this date.

historical_events.event_name: Temple like small structure was covered by brass
historical_events.event_description: Kṛṣṇa Lāla Maharjana Dhana Māyā Maharjana and their family covered a small, temple-like structure with brass. This was placed inside the Gaṇeśa temple on the New Year of NS 1113.
Two lion statues were donated by Darśanadhāri Rāma Jogī and Darśanadhāri Ramnātha Jogī. The location in which the statues were placed is not mentioned in the inscription.
Rājeśa Kapālī installed an oil-lamp balustrade in the Gorakhanātha shrine in memorandum of his late mother Dānamāyā Kapālī.
